question: How many tools does a delegated child see, now that managedSettings.allowedMcpServers:[] + allowManagedMcpServersOnly and per-agent disallowedTools:['mcp__*'] have landed — and is the Phase-1 gap (a background child at 625 tools vs the parent's 42) closed, narrowed or unchanged?
baselineCaveat: THE 625 HAS NO RECORDED APPARATUS in this tree — every occurrence is prose citing it (claude-builder.ts:753, claude-builder.test.ts:1467, the phase-1-1 plan at 787/819/853/1016); no result file, session log or probe produced it. The unnarrowed arm here IS the baseline re-measurement. Every 'gap' statement below is about THIS probe's two arms.

channels.strong: MCP REACHABILITY — engine-side/in-process, independent of the child's arithmetic: a PreToolUse firing carrying agent_id for an mcp__ name, a canUseTool consultation for an mcp__ name that no parent tool_use accounts for, or an mcp__ tool_use in the child's own engine-written transcript.
channels.weak: COUNTS — the child's self-reported census, written by the child to a file this process reads off disk. A model can abbreviate, miscount or hallucinate its own tool list; both the derived count and the model's stated TOTAL= are reported so degradation is visible.

gapThresholds.closed: narrowed child reports ZERO mcp__ tools, no MCP attempt is observed from inside it, and its total is ≤ 1.25 × the parent's OWN mid-session self-reported total
gapThresholds.narrowedButOpen: narrowed child total < 0.5 × unnarrowed child total, but not 'closed'
gapThresholds.unchanged: narrowed child total ≥ 0.9 × unnarrowed child total

census.note: NO CENSUS FILE. Nothing was measured through this channel.

notes: MEASURED. PARENT: 33 tools on the system/init envelope (MCP servers still 'pending' there, so MCP is excluded by construction) and 34 self-reported mid-session. NARROWED CHILD: 28 tools, ZERO of them mcp__, and no MCP call observable from inside it through any of the three engine-side channels. UNNARROWED CHILD, same prompt, same agent, same session shape, narrowing removed: 619 tools with 588 mcp__ names (mcpAttemptObserved=true) — so this instrument DOES see a wide child surface when there is one, which is what makes the narrowed reading a measurement rather than a silence. Gap assessment: CLOSED.
caveats: The two narrowings (session-level allowedMcpServers lock, per-agent disallowedTools) are applied and removed TOGETHER, as production ships them. Which one does the work is NOT separated by this probe and is not claimed.

Target agent trigger-dev-expert is one of only 3 of the owner's 144 on-disk agents with no `tools:` frontmatter allowlist. Whether a disk allowlist merges with Options.agents is UNMEASURED; if it binds, children of the other 141 are ~6 tools wide for a reason that has nothing to do with MCP, and this probe's numbers do not describe them.
The 625 was recorded for a BACKGROUND child. Both arms here run production's `background: false`. This probe does not reproduce that condition.
No sandbox block, unlike production — see the file header for why.

A session hit the 300s ceiling (narrowed=false, unnarrowed=true). The census is read off disk, so a timeout after the child wrote its file degrades the run rather than erasing it — but a truncated census reads as a smaller surface, which biases TOWARD a green. Weigh accordingly.
A child's stated TOTAL= disagreed with the number of names it actually wrote (narrowed: stated=28 derived=28; unnarrowed: stated=620 derived=619). Both are reported; neither is silently preferred.

parentCounts.timePointWarning: initToolCount is the engine's own count AT init, when every MCP server still reports status 'pending' (results/mcp.json) — it structurally EXCLUDES MCP tools. Only the mid-session self-reported counts are a like-for-like comparison with the child. Publishing 'parent 42 vs child N' without this line reproduces the artefact that most likely produced 625-vs-42 in the first place.

instrumentCalibration.note: Different time-points (init vs mid-session) and different sources (engine vs model), so a difference is expected. A LARGE one is a warning about how much weight the child counts can carry.

postRunAudit.addedAt: 2026-07-28, after the run, by a script that ADDS this key and changes no measured value
postRunAudit.why: Two fields in this file are misleading as written, and one number is absent. Saying so here is cheaper than letting the next reader re-derive it from the raw log.
findings: census.writtenByParent IS NOT AN AUTHORSHIP DISCRIMINATOR in SDK 0.3.220. This run measured that a SUBAGENT's tool_use blocks surface in the PARENT's assistant stream (the child's Write AND its mcp__github__get_me both appear in parentToolUses), so the field reads true for files the child demonstrably wrote. Read it as 'this name appears in the session tool_use stream'. It gates nothing.
child.mcpEvidence.canUseToolMcpNotAttributableToParent is structurally blind for the same reason and contributed nothing to either arm. The MCP reachability reading rests on the other two channels.

ATTRIBUTION THAT DID HOLD, engine-written and per-agent: PreToolUse firings carrying agent_id + agent_type='trigger-dev-expert' (recorded in both arms) and the child's own transcript at .../subagents/agent-*.jsonl (narrowed child: [Write]; unnarrowed child: [Bash, Write, ToolSearch, mcp__github__get_me]).

NEW, and it closes an item STATUS.md §3 lists as unverified: a PreToolUse hook DOES fire for subagent-originated tool calls. Probe E's four arms recorded firedInsideSubagent=false only because its children called no tools.

THE MCP DENY HELD — no external service was touched. The unnarrowed child's mcp__github__get_me returned a tool_result with is_error=true carrying this probe's own deny reason (read from the child transcript). canUseTool was NOT consulted for it: 0 MCP consultations in either arm.

UNOBTAINED NUMBER: the unnarrowed arm hit the 300s ceiling after the child's census was written but before the parent wrote its own, so parentCounts.unnarrowedArm.selfReportedCount is null. The unnarrowed child's 619/620-name census is complete (its TOTAL=/MCP_TOTAL= trailer is present), so the count itself is not truncated.

gateSelfTest.what: Before the live run, the detector->verdict->exit path was exercised with a synthetic message stream behind a module.register resolve hook. The shipped file was NOT edited.

cases.clean: PASS, exit 0 - the gate can say yes
cases.control-blind (unnarrowed child shows no: VOID, exit 1, narrowed arm never run - a small narrowed number cannot produce a green
cases.missing narrowed census: VOID, exit 1, INCONCLUSIVE - an absent census is not a narrow surface

censusArtifacts.coherenceCheck: The two child censuses agree on their NON-MCP part except for exactly three names, and all three are MCP plumbing: ListMcpResourcesTool, ReadMcpResourceDirTool, ReadMcpResourceTool (present unnarrowed, absent narrowed). Unnarrowed child = 31 non-mcp + 588 mcp__ = 619; narrowed child = 28. The narrowed PARENT's 34 is the narrowed child's 28 plus six parent-only tools (AskUserQuestion, EnterPlanMode, ExitPlanMode, ScheduleWakeup, TaskOutput, Workflow) - so under narrowing the child is NARROWER than its parent, which is the intended direction. This is a cross-check on the weak self-report channel: the differences between three independently written censuses are exactly the differences the mechanism predicts, which a fabricated list would not reproduce.

perAgentHalfIsUnexercisedInThisRun.finding: Probe G's narrowed arm ran with initMcpServerCount=0 and initMcpToolNames=[]. With no MCP tools in the session, per-agent disallowedTools:['mcp__*'] removed tools that were already absent, so THIS RUN CANNOT TELL A BOUNDARY FROM A NO-OP for production's second layer.
perAgentHalfIsUnexercisedInThisRun.resolvedBy: probes/results/G-PERAGENT.json (probe G2, 1 further live session, same day)
perAgentHalfIsUnexercisedInThisRun.answer: NO-OP. With the session-level lock removed and disallowedTools:['mcp__*'] kept, the child enumerated 620 tools of which 589 mcp__ - the same set as the unnarrowed child. Probe G's PASS rests ENTIRELY on managedSettings.allowedMcpServers:[] + allowManagedMcpServersOnly.

postRunAudit.shippedFileDiffersFromTheRun: After this run, probe-g-tool-surface.mjs gained COMMENT-ONLY edits: a header section recording what the run measured about the apparatus itself, and a docstring on parentWroteFile marking it as not an authorship discriminator. No logic and no output shape changed, so a reader diffing the file against this record will find prose only.
